# Import external resources into app-owned storage when direct access is unsuitable

## Platform difference

Copying selected content into the sandbox provides app-owned files; it does not grant continuing access to edit the original source.

## Implementation

Nexora stages a selected folder in native cache and copies it into app-owned workspaces with Rust-side size/count limits and symlink rejection. NipaPlay imports selected media with descriptor copies, temporary files and rename when directory access is unsupported. LocalSend resolves incoming URIs into readable cache files and derives response lengths from the resulting files before serving them.

## Applicability

Useful for native libraries that require ordinary file paths or for authorities/devices without suitable ongoing access. Cache and durable files directories have different retention semantics.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Explain duplicate storage and uninstall behavior to users. Large content should not be sent through a giant Dart channel payload just to copy it. LocalSend still has unsupported content-authority branches; a copy fallback is not universal URI support.

## Verification

Check copied bytes, capacity failures, interrupted copies, zero-byte files, path traversal/symlink inputs and cleanup; ensure the original folder is not advertised as a live synchronized workspace.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
